record.original_question: The number of abelian cube-free ternary words grows exponentially with length. Given a n-letter alphabet, deﬁne the sequence Zn recursively by: Z1 = 1 and Zn = Zn-1nZn-1, for every n > 1.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Two finite words u and v over a finite alphabet are said to be abelian equivalent if v is a permutation of u, i.e., each letter occurs the same number of times in u as in v. A word w contains an abelian cube if it has a factor of the form xyz where x, y, z are nonempty and pairwise abelian equivalent; otherwise w is called abelian cube-free.

Define the Zimin words over the alphabet of positive integers recursively by Z_1 = 1 and Z_n = Z_{n-1}\, n\, Z_{n-1} for every n > 1. A word w is said to encounter the abelian pattern Z_n if there exist nonempty factors w_1, w_2, …, w_k of w (where k is the number of variable occurrences in Z_n) realizing Z_n in such a way that any two factors corresponding to the same variable in Z_n are abelian equivalent.

Prove that the number of abelian cube-free words of length N over a 3-letter alphabet grows exponentially in N, i.e., establish the existence of a constant c > 1 and a positive constant C such that the count is at least C·c^N for all sufficiently large N.
artifact.status_search_result: Carpi (2004) proved that the number of ternary words of length n avoiding abelian cubes grows at least like r^n with r = 2^{1/24}, establishing exponential growth. The result is published in the Journal of Integer Sequences.

status_evidence.title: The Number of Ternary Words Avoiding Abelian Cubes Grows Exponentially
status_evidence.snippet: The number of ternary words of length n avoiding abelian cubes grows faster than r^n where r = 2^(1/24).
status_evidence.claim: Exponential growth of abelian cube-free ternary words has been proved.
